findings.claim: On a day with a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true for any slot inside the override before reaching busy.every(...), so existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored and the slot can be double-booked.
findings.evidence: `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` precedes the busy-time check; pre-patch code always ran the busy check. Applies to fixed-host (...schedule) and round-robin (...userSchedule) paths. Predicate-level repro in scratch repro.mjs (case 3) prints true; proposed getSchedule test: IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride + booking for user 101 at plus2 08:30Z-09:29:59Z, expect 08:30Z absent. Not run end-to-end (no deps).
findings.reason: Three correctness/spec seats agree independently, mechanism is a direct early return visible in source, and a predicate repro exists. Make red with the proposed getSchedule booking-on-override-day test.

findings.claim: Working-hours check uses workingHours.find(day matches && slot outside range), i.e. rejects a slot that is outside ANY range for that weekday instead of requiring it to be inside SOME range; split days and UTC-midnight-crossing schedules lose availability.
findings.evidence: getWorkingHours (packages/lib/availability.ts:62-127) splits hours crossing UTC midnight into two entries with overlapping days (e.g. America/Los_Angeles 9-17 Mon-Fri -> [1..5] 1020-1439 + [2..6] 0-60). Split hours 09-12 + 13-17 reject every slot. Now runs for every fixed host including all personal event types (isFixed: !schedulingType). Predicate repro cases 1 and 2 in scratch repro.mjs print true. Proposed test: single user, availability 09-12 and 13-17 UTC, expect slots; patched code returns none.
findings.reason: Independent agreement plus predicate repro; regression reaches every event type with a fixed host. Make red with split-hours getSchedule test.

findings.claim: In the working-hours check `end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so a slot that runs past the end of working hours is never rejected.
findings.evidence: `const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` duplicates `start`. Example: hours 9-17, 60-min event, 30-min interval: 16:30 slot passes though it ends 17:30.
findings.reason: All four seats flag it; the copy-paste is visible in source.

findings.claim: A date override is matched to slots by the UTC calendar date of its shifted start rather than the host's local date, and any same-UTC-date slot outside the override returns false; overrides near local midnight wipe out normal availability on the neighbouring day, and override slots on the other UTC date skip the override. Formatting via dayjs(...).format() in server-local mode against a UTC slot also makes the match depend on server TZ.
findings.evidence: Examples: UTC-7 host, override 18:00-20:00 Nov 17 -> Nov 18 01:00-03:00Z, so Nov 18 17:00Z normal slot rejected (repro.mjs case 4). Australia/Sydney override Jan 10 09-12 local -> Jan 9 23:00Z, rejecting most of Jan 9. IST unavailable override (00:00-00:00) on D -> D-1 18:30Z rejects all of D-1; proposed test snippet 2 in scratch override-ignores-busy.test-snippet.ts.
findings.reason: Three seats agree (one rated Critical; normalised to Important as it is timezone-dependent rather than universal). Predicate repro exists. Make red with snippet 2.

findings.claim: The override check uses dateOverrides.find with a side-effecting flag and returns 'unavailable' when the slot lies outside any one override range on that day, so a host with multiple override ranges on the same day (e.g. 9-10 and 14-15) gets no bookable slots that day.
findings.evidence: find callback sets outer dateOverrideExist=true and returns true when slot is outside the override; a 9:00 slot is outside the 14-15 range so find returns truthy and the slot is rejected. Same any-vs-some inversion as the working-hours finding. Reasoned; no test has two override ranges on one day.
findings.reason: Single advisory seat, but the mechanism is the same inversion three correctness seats confirmed for working hours at line 138; accepted. Make red with a two-range override test.

findings.claim: Override containment only rejects slots ending at/before the override start or starting after its end; a slot that starts inside and runs past the end (or starts exactly at the end, or starts before and ends inside) is accepted.
findings.evidence: Only slotStartTime.isAfter(end) is checked at the end boundary; should test slotEndTime. In round-robin this is the only per-host gate since getSlots builds the union of host slots: host with override 09:00-12:00 could be assigned 11:30-12:30. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Three seats (two Important, one Minor); boundary logic visible in source. Make red with a round-robin override-edge test.

findings.claim: getSlots corrects the override's time-of-day offset but activeOverrides still selects the invitee day using the organizer's wall-clock time stored as a fake-UTC instant, so the override lands on the wrong invitee day (fix half-applied).
findings.evidence: Example: Asia/Kolkata organizer, override D 02:00-05:00 IST, UTC invitee: selected for day D but shifted to 20:30-23:30, emitted on D when the real instant is D-1. Lines 206-208 unchanged by the patch. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Three seats identify the same root cause; reasoned. Make red with a getSlots/getSchedule test of an early-morning IST override viewed from UTC.

findings.claim: After applying the offset, startTime/endTime are computed as hour()*60+minute() with no day carry, so an override crossing the invitee's midnight yields endTime < startTime and buildSlots drops it; the user's working hours for that day were already removed, leaving zero slots (regression vs pre-patch).
findings.evidence: buildSlots skips `if (start >= end) continue` (line 68); working hours for override days removed at lines 228-243. Examples: America/New_York 09-17 override viewed from Asia/Kolkata -> 1110..150; IST 14-18 viewed from +12:00 -> 20:30-00:30. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Three seats agree; new regression introduced by the shift. Make red with a cross-midnight override test.

findings.claim: Scope gap: the title promises a timezone fix for overrides, but the patch newly enforces working hours and date overrides inside checkIfIsAvailable for every fixed and round-robin host (previously these spread-in fields were ignored), which is the source of the Critical regressions.
findings.evidence: Callers spread ...schedule / ...userSchedule (which carry workingHours and dateOverrides) into checkIfIsAvailable; pre-patch the function ignored them. isFixed: !schedulingType (line 369) means personal event types are affected.
findings.reason: Scope/intent question for the author with no spec to settle it; the concrete defects it causes are tracked as separate fix entries. Settle by confirming whether per-host enforcement in checkIfIsAvailable is intended.

findings.claim: dayjs(a) === dayjs(b) compares object identity and is always false, so the intended 'unavailable all day' (start == end) branch is dead.
findings.evidence: Two distinct Dayjs instances are never ===; should be isSame or removed.
findings.reason: All four seats; trivially verifiable from language semantics. Ponytail rated Important; normalised to Minor since getSlots masks it in practice.

findings.claim: dayjs(override.start.toString()) parses non-ISO Date#toString output (engine-dependent, drops ms) where dayjs(override.start) suffices; and TimeRange.timeZone is optional so .tz(undefined) silently uses the process timezone.
findings.evidence: packages/types/schedule.d.ts makes timeZone optional; only getSchedule passes overrides today, so latent.
findings.reason: All four seats; small, low-risk change.

findings.claim: The UTC offset is computed at the stored fake-UTC wall-clock instant rather than the real local instant, so it can be wrong on DST-transition dates (same in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots).
findings.evidence: Offset taken from tz() of the UTC-labelled stored time. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Edge case limited to DST-transition days; settle with a getSchedule test on a DST transition date for an affected zone (e.g. America/New_York second Sunday in March).

findings.claim: The only new test covers a single fixed user with no bookings for a second invitee timezone and reuses the +5:30 window (18:30Z) for Asia/Dhaka (+6:00); it does not exercise round-robin, busy times on override days, split hours, UTC-midnight-crossing schedules, or multiple override ranges, so none of the above defects would be caught.
findings.evidence: Lines 788-804; branch is fix/round-robin-date-override but no round-robin or loose-host test. PR template requires tests proving the fix.
findings.reason: All four seats; addressed by the red tests required for the accepted fixes.

findings.claim: The selected-slots checkIfIsAvailable call looks up userSchedule (line 579) and passes organizerTimeZone, but passes no dateOverrides or workingHours, so the lookup and prop do nothing and the find runs per slot per user for nothing.
findings.evidence: organizerTimeZone is only read inside dateOverrides.find, which defaults to [].
findings.reason: Deletion only; dead code verifiable from the call site.

findings.claim: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') is rebuilt four times in the override check; compute shifted start/end once per override.
findings.reason: Advisory; falls out naturally when rewriting the override check for the accepted correctness fixes.

findings.claim: dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset,'minute') chain built twice each for start and end; flatMap returns a single object and should be map.
findings.reason: Advisory; touched anyway by the day-carry fix at line 218.

findings.claim: organizerTimeZone duplicates the timeZone already spread in via ...schedule/...userSchedule, and is misnamed (it receives each host's timezone, not the organizer's); organizerUtcOffset in packages/lib/slots.ts:212 likewise.
findings.reason: ponytail: naming/duplication cleanup, non-blocking advisory; revisit when the override-check rewrite settles the function signature.
